newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fujitsu to set up computer centre in Canberra.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu to set up computer centre in Canberra.

text.p: The Australian unit of Japanese computer giant Fujitsu will set up a A$10 million Asia-Pacific desktop support centre in Canberra, creating 900 jobs, the Australian Government said on Monday.

Fujitsu Australia Ltd's Canberra facility would service Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines, Industry Minister John Moore said in a statement.
"The centre will offer a comprehensive range of consultancy and support services in the information technology and the telecommunications marketplace," he said.
Fujitsu, one of the world's largest computer companies, employs 167,000 people worldwide, including 2,500 in Australia.
Australia is seeking to encourage multinationals to base their Asia-Pacific operations here in a bid to boost local industry and create jobs.
